title: Petra and the Salt
premise: August Villalobos, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the ivory they carve, has survived the Thornfell mountains by being nobody: no guild, no name, no debts. When a dying courier presses a salt-stained map into their hands—a map to the Salt Court beneath the mountain, where souls are traded as currency—August learns the stranger was carrying proof that August's own soul was sold at birth by the family they never knew. Hunted by the court's salt-white enforcers and shadowed by a dead woman's voice only they can hear, August must cross every smuggler's road they swore never to walk again, gather three unlikely allies, and steal back their soul before the winter gates seal for a generation. In the end, August wins their soul back but chooses to leave half of it in the court's keeping as ransom for the other stolen dead, discovering that identity is not what you reclaim but what you give away—and returns to the surface changed, named, and finally belonging to themselves.
about_author: I. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former mountain-guide turned archivist who spent a decade cataloguing smuggler ballads in the Pyrenees before turning to fantasy. They write in unheated farmhouses and claim the cold improves the prose.

chapters.title: The Ivory Remembers
chapters.summary: POV August. In the border town of Lowmark, August carves a memorial whistle from a dead child's bone and hears the girl's last song, charging a grieving mother coin they don't need. The beat establishes August's gift as both livelihood and curse, and their fierce desire to remain unremarkable.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Salt Gate
chapters.summary: POV August. A frostbitten courier collapses in August's workshop, pressing a rolled hide map into their hands and gasping a name—Villalobos—before dying with salt crusted on her lips. August wants only to burn the map; instead they hide it as enforcers in white begin knocking on doors.

chapters.title: What the Dead Woman Wants
chapters.summary: POV August. The courier's voice begins speaking through every bone August touches, insisting the map leads to something that belongs to them. August flees Lowmark along the Widow's Stair, realizing invisibility is over, and the chapter ends on grief and denial rather than resolve.

chapters.title: The Toll of Thornfell
chapters.summary: POV August. On the high passes, August is caught by Brannoc, an exiled toll-keeper who once loved them, and must trade a secret for passage: the map's existence. The emotional beat is the ache of old loyalty versus new necessity, and Brannoc lets them go with a warning.

chapters.title: Salt on the Wind
chapters.summary: POV August. Pursued by a salt-white enforcer, August takes refuge with the Ashwife, a fire-witch who reads the map's wax seals and reveals its destination: the Salt Court beneath Mount Cindrel, where souls are minted into currency. First hint that August's own name appears on it.

chapters.title: The Name I Was Sold Under
chapters.summary: POV August. The Ashwife performs a reading on August's oldest carved bone and uncovers the truth: August's parents sold their newborn's soul to the court twenty-six years ago. August shatters the workshop, nearly burns the map, and the chapter closes on rage curdling into grim purpose.

chapters.title: Three Roads Down
chapters.summary: POV August. To enter the court, August needs a guide, a key, and a lie. They recruit Sefa, a disgraced salt-smuggler who knows the flooded mines, and bargain with the ghost of the courier, who agrees to be their voice inside if August carries her bones home after.

chapters.title: The Drowned Stair
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Shifting to the smuggler's POV, the descent through the flooded mines goes wrong when the water rises out of season—the court knows someone is coming. Sefa's guilt over a past betrayal surfaces, and the beat is trust tested under rising black water.

chapters.title: Where the Mountain Breathes
chapters.summary: POV August. The survivors emerge into vast caverns where the air itself tastes of salt and memory. August hears not one dead voice but thousands, the mined souls still echoing in the walls, and nearly loses themselves in the chorus before the courier's ghost anchors them.

chapters.title: The Court of White Ministers
chapters.summary: POV August. Disguised as a bone-merchant, August enters the Salt Court's antechamber and witnesses a soul-auction: a farmer's lifetime sold for a winter's grain. The beat is moral horror—August realizes the whole mountain economy runs on the dead poor.

chapters.title: An Old Debt, Newly Named
chapters.summary: POV August. In the court archives, August finds their own contract and a second signature: Brannoc witnessed the sale. Confronting this via a message sent up-mountain, August must decide whether betrayal by the man they loved changes what they owe him. Bitterness and doubt.

chapters.title: The Minister of Small Souls
chapters.summary: POV August. August bargains with Veyra, a minor minister who secretly hates the court, trading carving work—souls made audible in ivory—for access to the vault. The alliance forms uneasily; Veyra warns that reclaimed souls must be carried out in flesh or they evaporate.

chapters.title: Winter Falls Early
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Above, the first true snow seals the passes weeks ahead of schedule—the court's doing, to trap the thieves inside until spring. Sefa, waiting at the drowned stair, must choose between fleeing alone and holding the escape route open. Loyalty wins, barely.

chapters.title: The Vault of Voices
chapters.summary: POV August. Using Veyra's key, August reaches the vault: shelves of salt-glass jars, each humming with a life. They find their own jar—heavier than expected, warm like a sleeping animal—and, hearing the courier's daughter among the voices, cannot bring themselves to take only theirs.

chapters.title: Half a Soul
chapters.summary: POV August. Alarms rise as August lifts the jar. In the chaos they strike a desperate bargain with the vault itself, splitting their soul: half to carry free, half held as surety for the other stolen dead. The beat is sacrifice disguised as theft going wrong.

chapters.title: White Hands
chapters.summary: POV August. The enforcers corner August in the galleries; Brannoc arrives—not as rescuer but as the court's hired tracker, come to collect his debt. Their confrontation is the book's emotional pivot: he chose survival years ago and expects August to understand. August does not.

chapters.title: The Chorus Rises
chapters.summary: POV August. Fleeing with half a soul and a jar of others', August does what no thief has dared: plays the vault's voices aloud through carved bone, and the mined dead rise in resonance, cracking the court's foundations. The climax begins—the oppressed dead become the weapon.

chapters.title: Beneath the Breaking Mountain
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The escape through collapsing tunnels, told from Sefa's view as she holds the drowned stair against enforcers so August can pass. She settles her old betrayal by nearly dying for a stranger, and the two women finally speak honestly in the dark.

chapters.title: What Veyra Kept
chapters.summary: POV August. At the last gate, Veyra refuses to leave, staying behind to hold the ministers' attention—and asks August to carry out one small jar she never had the courage to steal herself. The beat is quiet devastation; some inheritances are chosen, not given.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: POV August. Surface-bound through the sealed passes, August releases the stolen souls into the snowstorm—the courier among them, her voice fading with gratitude. August keeps only their half-soul and the promise to return. Grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Carver's Mark
chapters.summary: POV August. In spring, August signs their first work with a real name—Petra Villalobos, the name on the sold contract, reclaimed—and opens a workshop that doubles as a sanctuary for the half-souled returning from the mountain. Identity rebuilt from choice, not birth.

chapters.title: Salt in the Doorway
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Final chapter: a line of salt on Petra's doorstep, the court's mark meaning we know where you live—and beside it, a small jar left in answer, containing the other half of her soul, returned unasked. Petra smiles, pockets her carving knife, and looks toward the mountain. Hope with teeth.
